note: The Python modules js/layer_a.js, js/image_meta.js, js/av_meta.js, js/stylometry.js and js/gumbel.js were ported from the upstream sources listed below. scripts/check-upstream.mjs compares the live content against these hashes. The parity suite proves the ported behaviour still matches for the cases it covers; this catches the rest: new options, new formats, anything the fixtures do not exercise. When one moves, re-port it and update `sha256` in the same commit.
followUp: If the parity suite is still green, the change is probably additive: a new format or option the fixtures do not reach. Add fixtures covering it, or the gap stays invisible the next time too.

sources.comment: Deliberately partial: upstream #156 hardened the error handling around the external c2patool subprocess (a failed run is inconclusive, not 'no C2PA'). There is no c2patool and no run_optional_tools in a browser, so js/image_meta.js has nothing to mirror there. Partial for the same reason since upstream 8e16b822, which passes creationflags=subprocess_creationflags to every subprocess.run so a child process opens no console window on Windows: a browser starts no child processes. Everything else in this file is ported. Partial in two more ways since 2026-08-27: upstream #252 refuses HTTP redirects in _synthid_score_http to block SSRF, and #254 adds a `changed` field to clean_image's returned dict for clean_file.py's new --only-changed flag. Neither has a browser counterpart: this port makes no HTTP calls, and clean() returns bytes rather than writing a file, so the caller already holds both sides to compare. Partial in one more way since upstream #261, which turns clean_image's post-clean scan into a residual scan: it adds an include_exiftool toggle to run_optional_tools/inspect_image, reuses synthid_before when no pixel remover ran, and lets inspect_image take pre-read bytes. A browser starts no exiftool subprocess, runs no SynthID scorer, and inspect() already takes bytes. Upstream #264 is ported in full: the C2PA ContentProvenanceBox user type d8fec3d6-1b0e-483c-9297-5828877ec481 is recognized and stripped in inspectIsobmff and stripIsobmff, so AVIF/HEIC and, through js/av_meta.js, MP4/MOV now lose a manifest whose payload carries no ASCII c2pa/jumb marker. Upstream #308 is ported in full: a zTXt/iTXt value that inflates past MAX_PNG_TEXT_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES (1 MiB) is refused rather than allocated, inspectPng reports the chunk as not fully inspected and stripPng drops it even in keep mode. The same commit swapped zlib.decompress for a decompressobj, so a stream that stops early now yields the prefix it decoded instead of nothing; js/image_meta.js's own inflate does the same, and keeps returning null for a stream that is corrupt rather than merely short. Partial in three more ways since 2026-09-01. #302 renamed the CtrlRegen and DiffusionPurification `strength` parameters to `intensity`: those are subprocess flags for pixel-domain removers a page cannot run. #201 added synthid_is_watermarked and made inspect_image report the SynthID verdict as a finding, which needs the scorer this port does not have. And run_synthid_score and _synthid_score_http gained a `data` parameter to skip a read-back, which is meaningless where inspect() is handed the bytes to begin with.

This port used to diverge here: upstream's _strip_moov_udta rebuilt an MP4 from the boxes that parsed and dropped everything after them, so a truncated download lost its media while the action list still said the tail was kept. Reported as guillaumemeyer/watermarks-remover#240 and fixed upstream by #242, which keeps the tail the same way and adds an inspection_incomplete flag that clean_av folds into still_has_ai_metadata. js/av_meta.js carries the same flag as inspectionIncomplete through both drivers, and tests/test_av_meta_parity.py now asserts the two agree. Partial in the same way image_meta.py is: inspect_av and clean_av take filesystem paths and use safe_write_bytes, which has no counterpart in a browser. clean_av's post-clean re-inspection is also not mirrored: the page inspects before cleaning and reports through the UI instead. Partial in one more way since upstream #254: clean_av's returned dict gained a `changed` field for clean_file.py's new --only-changed flag. cleanAv here returns the bytes rather than writing a file, so the caller already holds both sides to compare.

Ported in full apart from the command-line surface: print_human_stylometry_report and main() have no counterpart in a page, and score() returns the to_dict shape directly. Since upstream #258 a sample below MIN_SAMPLE_WORDS reports score and confidence_level as null rather than 0.0/CLEAN, and every report carries density_tier; matched markers carry spans as code-point offsets, which is why js/stylometry.js maps UTF-16 string indices back to code points before recording them.

Tracked as one definition, not as a file. classify_finding_confidence is the only thing js/stylometry.js mirrors from common.py, because StylometryReport.to_dict() calls it; the rest of common.py is filesystem and subprocess plumbing with no browser counterpart (read_text_input, backup_path, safe_write_bytes, the tool probes). Hashing the whole file would open a drift issue every time upstream touched any of that, and an issue that is usually noise is an issue nobody reads. Added after upstream #273 changed this function, classifying Layer A space homoglyphs as informational, and nothing here noticed.
